description: Bicycling, April 2007 - NAMED EDITOR'S CHOICE, Best Mountain Bike Under $1000 - "One tester exulted that 'a few years ago, you had to drop $1500-plus for a bike with hydraulic brakes, quality suspension and adjustable travel, but the Otero gives you all of that for a mere $750'. And while the other two bikes featured here are nicely equipped, it's save to say 'bikes at this price don't get any better than the 'Goose.' The Otero's Suntour fork and air-sprung shock 'far outshined the competition,' and it had the best brakes. We also noted that 'it's a stout climber and steers well.'" Mountain Bike Action, March 2007 - "The Otero gives you an adjustable leverage ratio rear suspension that is adjusted with the flip of a quick-release lever. This adjustment lets you firm or soften the way the rear suspension works. It also changes the travel from 2.5 inches to 4.4 inches. Think of it as two bikes in one at a great price." Bicycling Magazine, Dec 2006 - "Mongoose's Otero Super has features usually found on higher-level full-suspension bikes. There's an adjustable-travel swing-link suspension design paired with a lockout air-sprung shock. Suspension action is supple and smooth, with a controlled feel not often found at this price. And the fork, although just a touch behind in control and feel, is excellent. The Tektro hydraulic disc brakes are consistent, and we improved their power by moving the levers inboard of the shifters for maximum leverage. The hydraulic brakes will be strong as long as the pads stay fresh; the performance of mechanical discs falls off as cables become contaminated. SRAM's SX-5 shifters feel great and shift with accuracy in spite of the plastic triggers. While the Otero isn't light, its quality suspension makes it feel light, a big bonus. It rides with a solid feel that's missing in many sub-$1000 dualies. Mongoose's Otero Super isn't only a lot of bang for the buck, it's also an explosion of affordable technology for the budget-minded rider."
